text_fidelity_a:
Zink Polaroid Snap Instant Digital Camera (Pink) with ZINK Zero Ink Printing Technology This is a cameras that is perfect for some but not something that everyone will find useful. The ideal user is someone who wants a simple to use digital camera that has the ability to instantly print the photo without dealing with a PC or conventional printer. This does a pretty good job of accomplishing that goal. But, if you’re looking for a more advanced point and shoot with lots of image features, this may not be your best option.

The camera itself feels very solid, but lacks a key digital camera feature: a view screen. At first glance may seem to be a major omission. But, this camera is designed to be a high-tech replacement for the old-style Polaroid instant cameras by instantly (well, relatively instantly) printing the photo on Zink paper. Note that the paper needs to be purchased separately, and is pretty much an essential component for using the camera. While you can store photos on an SD card, the camera is really designed to be used with the Zink paper.

Usage is very straightforward – it’s about as point and shoot as you can get. That’s great for those who don’t want to fiddle with any settings, but it does put some constraints on image quality. I’ve had about 20% of my photos so far turn out less than ideal due to improper focus, poor white balance, poor resolution and/or incorrect color registration. That’s my major complaint with this camera – the paper is costly, and when you have to toss (or at least not really like) one in five photos, the cost can add up.

The images are small – the paper is only 2 by 3 inches. On the plus side it has a peel and stick backing, so you can use the photos as “post-its” very easily. Again, this is keeping with the intent of the camera, so I won’t downgrade the rating due to the small photo size.

Other negatives for me is that the battery is not user-replaceable. I’ve had too many electronic products with built-in batteries that had to be trashed since the internal battery no longer held a charge. I’m also not fond of the lens cap. It’s very easy to take off (it’s held in place by magnets) but there’s no attachment to the camera, so it’s very easy to misplace.

But this does score well with regard to ease of use and fun. As a test of ease of use I handed this to my Mom who is technically challenged, to say the least. She had no problems snapping photos and loved having the image print right there. She’s never liked using a digital camera in the past due to difficulty using it and dealing with image files. This was right up her ally.

While I’ll drop the rating to 4 stars due to the image quality issues that can crop up, overall this is a unique camera. It’s not right for everyone, but if you’re looking to revisit the days of the Polaroid instant camera while staying in the digital world, this is well worth considering.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Zink Polaroid Snap Instant Digital Camera (Pink) with ZINK Zero Ink Printing Technology

text_fidelity_a:
SABRENT 4TB Rocket NVMe PCIe M.2 2280 Internal SSD High Performance Solid State Drive (SB-ROCKET-4TB) So, I've had this thing for a few months, and it is no longer working. I put my OS (Win10) on it, and everything seemed fine. The NVMe has a heat shield on it that has a fan, so the temps never got as high as some people have reported.

However, the performance of my computer slowly declined until I could no longer rely on the computer to not crash randomly within 30 minutes of starting it. Everything was failing. I could not figure out what the heck was going on. Started troubleshooting everything. Couldn't get through a memtest, so I bought some new ram so I can use my computer while I wait for the G.Skill RMA process. However, even with the new ram, the PC cannot boot with the Sabrent NVMe. Does not proceed further than the loading screen.

Tried booting into safe mode, which failed, as well as resetting the computer through the windows troubleshooting tool. Nothing would go past the loading screen. I've added another photo showing that substantial loss of performance, even while it is not being used by anything else. Keep in mind that although the numbers are mostly higher than the SATA SSD, a loss in performance like this is a tell-tale sign that it is failing. If you notice something similar with your hardware, back up what you want to keep immediately.

Tried booting from my older SSD, and was able to boot just fine. I am still somehow able to access the information on the NVMe when booting from another SSD, but the system is unstable while running on it. I will continue to try to get a replacement or a refund before conceding that I have a $120 tax for trying to save money.

I tried to use the tool to check if there was a firmware update. Doesn't work, as it said cannot find information on the hardware. This is with the latest everything. Seemed odd, so I sent an email to the bug reporting email they provide. Got a response from google saying that email does not exist....

I reached out to Sabrent technical support. No response after a week.

I'm very disappointed. I've gotten other sabrent hardware before and hadn't had problems. Looks like their memory is not their game. Even worse that their customer support is non-existent. Don't expect to get help if you run into the same issue that I got.

I'd recommend spending the extra $20 or $30 to get hardware that has a record of reliability, like samsung (the much older SSD that still works, and and using right now to be able to even use my computer is the 840 EVO).
text_fidelity_b: SABRENT 4TB Rocket NVMe PCIe M.2 2280 Internal SSD High Performance Solid State Drive (SB-ROCKET-4TB)

Kindle Oasis E-reader (Previous Generation - 9th) - Graphite, 7" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Waterproof, Built-In Audible, 8 GB, Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers (Closeout) Some people have claimed the screen is square, it's not. Like all previous Kindles this is measured diagonally. It only appears square because the one side of the bezel with the buttons (also not loud as has been claimed and the touch screen works fine if the nearly inaudible click might keep a partner awake).
I really like the seven inch screen and design of this new Kindle it's much closer to a regular paperback page now. I do wish the boldness option was allowed to be applied to any book and not just those purchased from Amazon. I get plenty of books from other sites such as Baen and Project Gutenberg but they're not given the full functionality Amazon's books are. I don't think it's fair.
The weight and balance. In or out of the cover is almost perfect. I find I can comfortably read for hours and if either hand gets tired a quick flip and you're reading with the other. I've reversed the page turn buttons like on the old K3/Kindle keyboard the page forward button is more natural feeling if it's at the bottom I have no idea why Amazon has the default reversed. Holding it you're more apt to go forward than bsck plus if you need to go back you can just slide your finger towards the screen and use the touch screen to go back, then it's right back to the lower button to continue reading. I rather like this device. It's noy light years ahead of the Voyage or PaperWhite but it is certainly a few large steps ahead. I haven't and have no plans to test the waterproof claims. I like the idea because I'm disabled and on a walker my previous Kindles have gotten damp. Now i don't have to worry. I did pour a few drops of water on the cover. All but one rolled off. The one soaked in. Caveat emptor. Im happy with the purchase so far. It was a gift to myself for having quit smoking for 10 full years. I deserved it.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis E-reader (Previous Generation - 9th) - Graphite, 7" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Waterproof, Built-In Audible, 8 GB, Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers (Closeout)

text_fidelity_a:
SABRENT Rocket Q 500GB NVMe PCIe M.2 2280 Internal SSD High Performance Solid State Drive R/W 2000/1000MB/s (SB-RKTQ-500) Compared to the Crucial 1TB M2 NVME I reviewed earlier, this Sabrent 512GB model benchmarks a little faster. And it works just fine on a PCI M2 adapter card, which are only a few bucks. (I bought the cheapest one available and it works.)

The NVME still offers much faster R/W speeds than other drives even when used with SATA 1 (as on my workstation). For example, the SSD I was using as my hard disk benchmarks at about 220MB/second. The Sabrent NVME on a PCI card benchmarks at about 1.5GB/second.

This time I experimented to see if I could get Debian Linux distro running on the NVME on my older workstation.

It took a few tries. Getting the OS to boot directly from the NVME was a no-go. Since the NVME is mounted on an adapter card, I had hoped it would trick the system into thinking it was just an ordinary SATA drive and boot from it. But that didn't happen.

So what I did was installed all the Linux OS EXCEPT for the boot folder on the NVME, and put the boot folder on the SSD HDD. So it boots from the SSD but the entire OS is on the NVME and runs from it.

Step one:

The partition manager in the Debian installer didn't want to partition the NVME at first.

So I bailed out of it and used GParted (Gnome disks utility couldn't do this) to "create partition table" and selected msdos as type. That wiped everything and turned the whole drive into unallocated space. From that point the partition manager worked.

Step two:

From the linux bootable USB installer I partitioned the SSD (not the NVME) with a primary partition labeled (to be mounted) as /boot. (You can make this partition most any size from a few GB on up---the boot files don't require a lot of space.) The remaining space I manually labeled as /msc.

I partitioned the NVME so the installer would put everything else on it, starting with / (root). You can simply make the whole NVME / root and the installer will take care of putting everything else on that drive, or you can do what I did and set up size-defined partitions for /home, /usr, and so on.

After installing the system, the installer asks where you want the bootloader GRUB installed. I selected the SSD.

It worked. The SSD does the booting to the NVME, which then runs the OS. And it did improve speed.
text_fidelity_b: SABRENT Rocket Q 500GB NVMe PCIe M.2 2280 Internal SSD High Performance Solid State Drive R/W 2000/1000MB/s (SB-RKTQ-500)

It holds a charge for at least 2-3 days of active homework use and general internet fun for me. It starts up almost instantly when I open it! The screen size is fine, and I often have two windows open at the same time, side by side. I've been trying to read more articles online without printing them, and using online textbooks via my Kindle app. After a bit of a learning curve, this has worked out awesome, because if I have my Chromebook, I have ALL my textbooks with me, plus my course information, and my notebook to write things down. I love it. Plus, it doesn't get hot or make a whirring sound when you use it for a long time. I like that because I often use mine while I"m sitting on the couch.

Getting used to using the Chromebook had some hiccups. First, I recommend using Google Docs for writing because it has an offline mode. The Windows OneDrive and cloud version of Word works ok, but if your internet has any interruption, you can't keep typing. That's annoying. So use Google Docs, and don't worry about it! (But if you're working on a project with someone, and they use Word on a Windows laptop, you can collaborate with them no problem using the cloud version of Word.) Second, organizing my files confused me, until I realized that "Save As" is now "Move to folder.' Also, you can download a few files to your Chromebook, so if you need to upload an attachment to Blackboard, you can pretty easily. You'll use your Google Drive for much of your file storage. I did connect my OneDrive to my Chromebook, but it's through a third party app thing, and the connection always has to be redone, so I don't really rely on that, and I plan to move my OneDrive stuff to my Google drive soon.

The only thing that was really hard was setting up my Chromebook to print to my WiFi printer. Google cloud print is in beta, and in theory, it's awesome. When you're done setting it up, you could print to your home printer from anywhere, using your mobile device. However, Google your printer and how to set up cloud print, and give yourself some time to set it up. If you're in a rush, you should just plug your printer into your Chromebook.

Lastly, since many public schools are going Chromebook, I thought it was a good idea to get one myself. I'm working on getting my Master of Arts in Teaching to be an elementary/middle school teacher. Using one for my own schoolwork helps me be able to help students use their Chromebooks. Additionally, the price is so nice, I don't worry about having to ever replace my Chromebook, because if it was damaged by schoolchildren, I'd only be out about $160 (instead of $2000 for a Mac). I'm even thinking of getting one for my mom, since most of what she does online could be done on a Chromebook, too.

Oh, and one very last thing, the keyboard is really enjoyable to type on. The keys are spaced comfortably, and the individual keys make a nice clicky sound, are springy, and are nice and thin, for fast typing. I know that might sound weird, but I'm picky about my keyboards.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Chromebook, 11.6-Inch, CB3-111-C670 (Intel Celeron, 2GB, 16GB SSD, White) **Discontinued by Manufacturer**

text_fidelity_a:
Creative Zen Sleek Photo 20 GB Multimedia Player (Aluminum/White) I was in the market for a hard drive-based music player and didn't want to go the normal iPxx route, so I began checking into different brands. I had a list of criteria that the player had to meet:

-EXCELLENT SOUND. This is critical. A SnR (Signal to Noise Ratio) of 95db or better

-Excellent battery life. At least 15 hours

-At least 20 GB

-A color screen

-Sturdy build

-As little touch-sensitive controlling as possible. Click wheels are inaccurate and bothersome.

-Ease of use. Drag and drop is preferred.

-AC adapter for charging on the road or from an AC converter in a car

This player meets all of those needs. The SnR is 97db, I've gotten 18 hours out of the battery (remember that increased settings like equalizers and higher bitrates mean lower battery life for ALL players), the case is solid and brushed aluminum, the screen is pretty and quite sharp, only one touch-sensitive control is present, the player CAN drag and drop through Win XP, and it comes with a wall adapter.

I love the powerful sound this puts out and it can drive my big headphones with no problem. It can, like most HDD players, set aside a partition for storage. It has a good FM tuner, recording of FM and a little mic for voice notes. It can even sync with Outlook for contacts and other info. The hard disk seems fast and

Now for the drawbacks:

-You can't watch 15fps video on a tiny screen and reduce your battery life by 67%

-The USB cable is proprietary...no mini USB!

-The wall charger cable plugs into the USB cable...this means two cables for recharging from the wall

-Looking at photos and playing music at the same time is not possible

-Creative software is always iffy. Thankfully, in Win XP, you can open the player from My Computer and access its contents directly with non-DRM music and photos.

-Battery is NON-USER REPLACEABLE. This is odd for Creative.

-No mention of this on the Creative website. Thankfully, updated drivers ARE available from support.

This player would have been state-of-the-art about a year ago, but has been eclipsed by its bigger brother the Zen Vision with 30 and 60GB drives and video...however, if you're not buying into the "kill your eyes with tiny video on tiny screens" and just want a SOLID and RELIABLE player with booming sound, this is it!!! You can tell it's custom-made for Windows (it's MTP, not UMS for any computer), but if you're running XP, then it's a solid choice because you can skip the Creative software and just load music on it.

If you can get it on sale like I did, snatch it up. This is a little gem of a player!
text_fidelity_b: Creative Zen Sleek Photo 20 GB Multimedia Player (Aluminum/White)

LotFancy Laptop Cooler Cooling Pad with 5 Quiet Fans for 12-17" Notebook, Dual USB Ports A good laptop chiller pad becomes important when you run a lot of graphics-intensive games or if you are doing anything requiring the CPU to run a heavy load. Heat is the enemy of a computer system and the fastest way to a dead laptop is to not deal with heat issues when there’s a problem. I had a chill pad some time ago and it was sub-par. This one by LotFancy is much better and it does a good job.

First off, this is a big chill pad, the same basic dimensions as my laptop but much thicker. I have a 15.6" laptop and this pad is almost a perfect and exact fit, with only a narrow area in the back that extends past the end of the laptop. If you want a small and petite chill pad, this is not the one you want. It does incline too with a metal bar and slots in the case so that the laptop can be angled up. This actually is good for exposing it to even more air.

This chill pad connects to a USB port so it can either be plugged into a port on the computer or into a hub. There are two ports on it and both seem to be the same in terms of how the pad operates. That is, the pad operates at the same speed regardless of which port is used. There are also two buttons on the pad for turning it on. One turns on the larger fan in the middle, and the other turns on all the other fans. Two green LEDs next to those buttons indicate that the pad is powered on and working.

This pad moves a lot of air and it does a good job of cooling the laptop. But, it does so very quietly which is a huge plus. I have it set up in my home office and the pad makes about as much noise as a desktop computer, maybe a little less. The sound it makes is a gentle hum.

When powered on each fan has a bright blue LED in it. While they look cool when there’s no laptop on the pad, they’re all but invisible when the laptop is sitting on top. There isn’t even much of a glow coming from the pad. I turned on the pad, turned out all of the lights and the glow from the laptop screen was enough to overpower any light that might have come from the pad. Except for the low hum I wouldn’t know it was even turned on.

This is a good chill pad. It works quietly and it moves a lot of air. Compared to other chill pads I have used this one is very good and I am happy to recommend it.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: LotFancy Laptop Cooler Cooling Pad with 5 Quiet Fans for 12-17" Notebook, Dual USB Ports

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm Instax Wide 300 Instant Film Camera (Black) Boy! does this camera remind me of my old Polaroid Square Shooter. This camera is NOTHING like your iPhone camera as it's big, and totally analog except for the film counter on the back. I love it when the motor runs and film comes sliding out - a sound I well remember. I think the hardest thing about using this camera was getting the shoulder strap put on, other than that it's very easy to use. Though it is on the big side, it doesn't weigh much and the view finder and shutter button are pretty much intuitive. I'm left handed so holding it like a right-hander took a little getting used too, but it's not a problem for me. This camera is made for right-handers so those who are very much left-handed might not like the way you have to hold it, and the shutter button is on the right side front. It has flash and you can adjust the light/dark and distance to you subject with minimal effort.

Loading the film was easy, aiming at my subject was easy, the shutter button was easy to depress and everything is/was easy. The close-up adapter looks like there's no way it will attach itself to the lens, but somehow it does. I took one close-up of my dog but the picture didn't turn out very good because she moved away right when I hit the shutter button-but that's typical for her. I haven't taken a "selfie" yet but it seems like it will be easy to do.

The color development of the film is pretty good. I took a wide angle picture of my raised garden beds and I was able to get all of them in the picture and the various green colors were vivid. I also took a picture of the front of our house, and though I had to still walk across the street to our neighbor's driveway to get the entire house in the view finder, the picture turned out nice. Again, the colors were bright and vivid. It got the entire house plus some area on both sides. In the past with my other cameras I would have to get further away or be happy with just most of the house in the picture so it's real nice to get the whole thing with room to spare.

The film is kind of pricey. For a pack of 40 pictures it costs around $34.00. I figured it would be kind of expensive and I hope the price of the film goes down some. This is a comfort camera for those of us who grew up with Polaroids. It may be that since we are living in highly uncertain and stressful times, having a camera like this is a cool blast from the past and may make us just feel better having one like this, plus it takes nice pictures.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm Instax Wide 300 Instant Film Camera (Black)

XBOOM Mini Portable Capsule Speaker with Rechargeable Battery and Enhanced Bass+ Resonator (Mini - Black) -1 pack When listening to your favorite tunes, videos, etc., sound enhancement makes a noticeable difference. Cell phones and other electronic devices are often quite lacking in sound quality, mainly because the sounds are directed to a tiny speaker. An enhancement can make music and other noises come to life and the Xboom Mini Portable Capsule Speaker is ready to serve in this regard.

This speaker is small, stylish, and versatile and I have used it with several different electronic devices. It is very compact in size, operates on a rechargeable battery, and can be collapsed to a size so small that it fits into tight quarters with ease. Just plug it into a cell phone, tablet, or other device, flip the switch, adjust the volume, and listen to your favorite music like never before.

I was skeptical when I first used this device because it just didn’t seem capable of much. It looks cool, but it’s just so small. How much sound could possibly release itself from such a tiny speaker, I wondered. But a few uses demonstrate that this little speaker is capable of many great things. It doesn’t produces deafening decibels, no. But the volume is much louder than that of a typical cell phone or tablet. And the bass enhancement makes it sound like a true stereo speaker. I was pleasantly surprised when I used it and I couldn’t believe something so seemingly miniscule and insignificant would be capable of so much.

The battery in this little guy is good for about 12 hours of use, according to the manufacturer. Truth is, I have never had to worry about this because, if you use the USB cord and plug into a computer, you don’t need to charge it first. My kids like to use it in their cell phones and they are always careful to maintain the charge. Twelve hours is a long time and the reason I know it’s a long time is because, in a few months of use, it has never exhausted its charge. The kiddos can use it on a lengthy road trip and it maintains its juice.

Many smaller electronics need better sound and the Xboom Mini Portable Capsule Speaker is a very good device for improving your next audio experience. Multiple units can be plugged together for even greater satisfaction but even if you have only one, you will find this little gadget is more than able to deliver very good sound quality. It’s one of my favorite electronic enhancers and one I and my kids will continue to use.

text_fidelity_a:
Sony MDRNC8/WMI Noise Canceling Headphone, White I thought "They're cheap, why not?" I expected that Sony would at least make a semi-descent product, but I was wrong. They only cut out about 5% of ambient noise. I tested them in a lot of different environments and it didn't perform well under any circumstance.

I compared them to a pair of low-end headphones ($20) to set a baseline, see below.

Test:
In flight - no noticeable difference between each pair
While driving - slightly better muffling of midrange noise, but slight (2% better)
Fan on high & low - slightly better canceling of low freq noise (2% better)
In crowed auditorium - slight better muffling (1% better)

They barely did any better than the cheap-o, non-noisecanceling, over the ear headphones I got for half the price.

The biggest thing I noticed is that the very little amount of noise that was actively cancelled was replaced fully by a hissing sound. This made the headset pretty much useless.

I would recommend not buying these headphones. I returned the set I bought, and got my money back. There are better headsets at this price.
text_fidelity_b: Sony MDRNC8/WMI Noise Canceling Headphone, White

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Gear IconX (2018 Edition) SM-R140NZKAXAR Bluetooth Cord-free Fitness Earbuds, w/ On-board 4Gb MP3 Player (US Version with Warranty) - Black I’m NOT an audiophile, but I was blown away by the sound quality delivered by these SAMSUNG GEAR ICONX (2018 Edition) BLUETOOTH CORD-FREE FITNESS EARBUDS (w/On-board 4Gb MP3 Player; Gray (SM-R140NZAAXAR)). I like classical music, and the sound is so relaxing and immersive, I forget that I’m wearing earbuds. (It helps that these are totally without wires, of course.)

The earbuds are far and away the most comfortable that I’ve ever worn. You get three sizes of in-ear tips (S, M, L). There is NO sound leakage to speak of. The touch controls for music work fine, though it takes some practice to master the double- and triple-taps (sound tracks) and swipes (volume) so that you get consistent results. For me, it’s easiest to play an album or list at a set volume, without fussing with the controls.

I didn’t test the call-answering features or other features beyond playing music. The earbuds paired, without incident, with my iPad Pro and with my Samsung Galaxy S7 Edge. The charging case seems to need to be charged up to the green light for pairing to work.

A great feature is that you can copy music files to the earbuds. They have 4GB of built-in storage. This means you don’t have to stay within Bluetooth range of your mobile device to play music.

Three stars because I haven’t used the earbuds consistently for a full month. As much as I love these, I’m afraid that the left earbud will fail before long (as other reviewers have reported).

Already the left earbud has exhibited signs of NOT charging properly. With the case closed and plugged in (and with brand-new earbuds), the left charging light blinked red, which indicates “not charging”. I corrected the problem by opening the case and reseating the left earbud in the cradle, but of course I’m wondering whether there is a more serious problem that will surface soon.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Gear IconX (2018 Edition) SM-R140NZKAXAR Bluetooth Cord-free Fitness Earbuds, w/ On-board 4Gb MP3 Player (US Version with Warranty) - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Arteck 2.4G Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo Ultra Compact Slim Stainless Full Size Keyboard and Ergonomic Mouse for Computer/Desktop/PC/Laptop and Windows 10/8/7 Build in Rechargeable Battery ARTECK HW086MW162 Wireless Keyboard and Mouse combo, still charging that's why there are cables. Pen in the photo for size reference, along with the box it came in.

Unboxing was “frustration free” as advertised. I recycled my Logitech cord that connected to my desktop and inserted the USB receiver in it and it worked.

I plugged in the Micro USB charging cable to the keyboard and mouse. Only one Micro USB charging cable came with the combo so I used an extra Android Micro USB charging cable to charge both at the same time.

I was able to use the keyboard and mouse in a few moments. My computer automatically updated the files needed in a few minutes.

All in all the unboxing and set up was quick and effortless. Now I am going to explore the keyboard.

This keyboard has no number side keyboard that makes it smaller.

It has a blue function key to access page up, page down, home, and end, on the lower right where the left, right, up, down keys are.

Along the top with the F keys are blue function commands:

Escape has “Media” – when pressed opened Wave Pad, a NCH program I have installed.

F1 has an >/||, which did nothing when pressed

F2 has |<<, which did nothing when pressed

F3 has >>|, which did nothing when pressed

F4 has a speaker symbol )x, That mutes sound

F5 has a speaker symbol - which lowers volume

F6 has a speaker symbol + which increases volume

F7 has a symbol for home, which opens a new browser tab

F8 has a symbol of a magnifying glass that opens a search side window and uses Bing for search, when I clicked on one of the search results it opened a new Chrome tab. I had Chrome already opened.

F9 has a symbol for a folder, which did nothing when pressed

F10 has a symbol for power which turned off my computer. Since I had programs opened my computer asked for permission so I canceled.

F11 has “insert” on it which is pretty self explanatory

F 12 has “PrtSc” for print screen

The action on the keyboard is nice and a lot quieter than the Logitech keyboard I am replacing. The mouse action is good and also quiet.

For less than $23 this is a good keyboard and mouse. I never used the number keys on the side of my Logitech keyboard, which needed batteries, as did the mouse that came with it. The mouse had begun to do double clicks when I clicked once and the keyboard “enter” would stay down. That's why I replaced them for this Arteck Keyboard and Mouse combo. To be able to stop buying and replacing batteries and the small space it takes up, along with it is quiet, makes my money well spent.
text_fidelity_b: Arteck 2.4G Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo Ultra Compact Slim Stainless Full Size Keyboard and Ergonomic Mouse for Computer/Desktop/PC/Laptop and Windows 10/8/7 Build in Rechargeable Battery

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm Instax Mini 26 + Rainbow Film Bundle - Black A long time ago I had access to a Polaroid Instamatic camera. It was great - snap a picture, it spits out a sheet. Wait about 2 minutes and what you have is a printed photograph. Polaroid is gone now (though the name gets licensed over and over again), and with it went all of the film for the camera that made it so useful. This new camera by Fuji brings back some of the fun of instant photos, though it is by no means perfect and it suffers from some of the same issues the older Polaroid camera had.

The idea is very straightforward - point-and-shoot, and the camera ejects an exposure that will develop over a few moments and will be fully developed in approximately 2 minutes. This is great for social events and is a fun way to share candid shots. The camera is very lightweight and it is small too so it is easy to pack and carry with you.

There are a few issues with the camera, though, some of which are very much like the old Polaroids of days gone by. The images do come out a bit grainy and are definitely not high resolution. If you are looking for images with nice, clean edge detail and bright, vibrant colors, this is going to disappoint you. Also, the images are really small, a little bigger than a passport picture but not by very much. And finally, the film is relatively expensive, a pack of exposures coming with only 10 slides and costing about $0.60 per exposure.

On the plus side, the camera is very easy to use and the camera body itself is not very expensive at all.

There are trade-offs with this camera. On one hand, it is super convenient, it’s fun and it’s relatively inexpensive. However, exposure quality is mediocre, pictures are small and on a per-picture basis the exposures are somewhat expensive. To me, the fun factor weighs heavily in favor of this camera and offsets some of the negatives. For social gatherings and recreational events, this is a fun camera and will serve well. Do not expect to have high-end results, though.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm Instax Mini 26 + Rainbow Film Bundle - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Canon EF-S 55-250mm f/4.0-5.6 IS II Telephoto Zoom Lens I'm very pleased with this lens given the price. Although it won't give a Canon L lens a run for its money, it's reasonable fast and has a nice range. The build quality is very good for this price point. Both the zoom movement and focusing are smooth. The zoom marking are well-marked. While the mount is plastic rather than metal, this keeps the lens weight down, which is always something that I appreciate. Despite being plastic the mount and housing are more than sturdy enough for even the most avid amateur photographer.

The image stabilization works very well and is an essential feature to have unless you have rock-steady hands.

I find the image quality to be excellent at all zoom ranges except for when it's at its max range, but even then it's more than acceptable.

It's certainly not the best lens that Canon makes, but I don't think there's another zoom out there that can match this performance at this price. It's a great second lens if you have a crop sensor body (such as the Rebel series) and the 18-55mm zoom (which is a common kit lens). The pair provides a wide range of shooting opportunities at a very reasonable cost. Highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF-S 55-250mm f/4.0-5.6 IS II Telephoto Zoom Lens

text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link AC750 Wireless Wi-Fi Gigabit Router (Archer C2) I am not super "techie" like some of the other folks reviewing this router, just your average housewife who likes gadgets and tries not to drown in the constant wave of weekly tech improvements. As such, I wanted a new router to replace our two year old dual band Belkin with similar speed output, but only a single antenna. The Belkin had a number of dead spots despite using one of those extender things and I had had enough. Enter this TP-Link router.

I was wary of the installation after seeing some other reviews and the difficulties folks have been reporting. However, after reading the box and the instructions fully FIRST and then following the directions exactly, I had no problems. One thing I did notice immediately, is this router is meant to be used with a cable modem and that modem must be powered off before you connect it to this router. I used the website installation method and was up and going in a total of 20 minutes - that is from opening the box to having all our wireless stuff connected to the internet again. The website management page is very detailed and allows for a lot of customization of your network, honestly, more than I need or understand. But changing the router's password and setting our network name was simple and worked on the first try.

After three days of use I like it. The speed is decent and the dual antenna set up has improved the coverage problem we were having with the old Belkin router. I haven't experienced any slowdown or degradation of connectivity with multiple devices going at once thus far. A Fire Phone surfing the net, Fire tablet streaming music, laptop doing email, and a smart tv streaming video all at once in different rooms. So...a good router for every day family use in a pretty typical home.

*********** UPDATE FEBRUARY 2015 ***********
After 90 days this router is trouble free and really working like a champ. Our cable company upgraded our modem and increased our internet speeds recently, requiring a full shutdown and reconnect of my entire network. It was a snap and the router has had no problem with faster connection and the new modem. I relocated everything to the center of our house when everything was being swapped out and the router is now sending a five bar signal out to the back deck, which means I can sit out there with the dogs in nice weather to do email etc.

*****************UPDATE APRIL 2016 *************

I'm still using this router every single day for literally every single WiFi device in our house and it just does its job with zero drama every day. We now have two tablets, two smartphones, three DVR boxes on WiFi, two laptops, a printer, a Fire Stick for streaming movies, a smart tv connected the web now and then, and the Echo that's connected all the time. (yeah, I know...we watch a LOT of television in this house!)

Right this minute I am streaming music on the Echo, recording tv shows on two different DVR boxes, using my laptop to update this review, and uploading 42 photos from my phone to the cloud and pushing email to my tablet. Oh - and I am sitting outside on the patio enjoying the lovely spring day. This router is powerful and I have no dead spots inside or out in the backyard.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link AC750 Wireless Wi-Fi Gigabit Router (Archer C2)

Surge Protector Power Strip - Flat Plug Extension Cord, TROND 8 Widely-Spaced Outlets, 4 USB Charger(1 USB C Port), 5FT Ultra Thin Cord, 1440J, Flat Wall Plug, Desk Charging Station for Travel, White The TROND Flat Plug Power Strip Surge Protector is a great concept. Everything about it shows that some thought has been given to its design. Unfortunately, their choice of materials weren't as well thought out.

Some design concepts that attracted me to this surge protector is that it gives you 8 power plugs in a surface area that's just under 4 x 4 inches. The four plugs at the top are grounded while the 4 on the side are two-prongs. In addition, the wall plug is flat, giving you a lot of options as to where you can plug this product in. Finally, there are three USB-A ports and one USB-C port.

However, as I've mentioned, some design choices are questionable. As with many surge protectors, the USB ports are under-powered. The Type-A ports are not too bad at 5V/2.4A, but there is no quick charge capability. The Type-C is not PD, so your charging options are no better than the Type-A ports. You're stuck with 5V/3A with a total wattage shared between them at 14W or 3.4A.

My second gripe is with the build material. Compared to many power strips, the plastic covering this product feels quite cheap. It has a smooth texture and just feels... thin to the touch. The same plastic also covers the wall plug. In addition, the power wire is thinner than other power strips that you'll find. They feel more like the two-prong extension cords, except that it has three wires.

Now, I don't have proof that their choice of materials will be an issue at all, but it does give me pause.
text_fidelity_b: Surge Protector Power Strip - Flat Plug Extension Cord, TROND 8 Widely-Spaced Outlets, 4 USB Charger(1 USB C Port), 5FT Ultra Thin Cord, 1440J, Flat Wall Plug, Desk Charging Station for Travel, White

text_fidelity_a:
Case Logic DCB-308 SLR Camera Sling (Black) I have been using this sling for some time now. When I received this sling I was seriously looking at buying the [[ASIN:B0036AWR8E Lowepro SlingShot 202 AW]] and I think for my purposes, this is the better sling for me. The one thing I did not like about the Lowpro was that it was broken up into two compartments which limited my ability to put my Canon 200-400 5.6 zoom in it comfortably. The large main compartment easily, but snugly holds my 40D and lense, which room to spare to include a wide angle.

As for slings in general. I have a Tamarac backpack which I love, but tend to way over pack (because I can.) It is bulky and awkward to wear, but does have a hip belt to take the weight off the shoulders. Also, I tried a holster style case, but it never felt secure and I never trusted my camera and lense in such a flimsy case. The sling, once in place seems to become a part of my body while hiking and climbing. It feels more secure than the backpack and far more secure than the holster.

Good Points

- nice spacious compartment for a DSLR and Zoom lense
- Sturdy with strap across you chest, it feels very secure on.
- Rotating the sling gives a sturdy platform to remove or insert camera.
- It is not big enough to overpack
- plenty of space for battery, charger, cards, notebook or guide, and two lenses and body
- Rain cover is nice addition (have not used it, but love the extra insurance.)
- Well padded
- Nice construction, classic design.
- Nice side handle for carrying when not slung.

Bad Points

- Sling Accentuates Man-boobs (I've tried several different ways of placing the strap, but it seems the only fix is portion control and moderate exercise.)
- no hip belt so weight is held on shoulders for long hikes, but weight is limited somewhat by size.

All in all, I have to admit I have come to love this sling. It has traveled with me quite a bit and I trust it to hold my treasured camera and lense. Easy to pack and will handle the essentials. It is cheaper than the Lowe sling in price, but not functionality. I recommend this to anyone who wants to pack in a DSLR.
text_fidelity_b: Case Logic DCB-308 SLR Camera Sling (Black)

SABRE Home Security Personal Safety Kit, Comes With A 120 dB Doorstop Alarm, 120 dB Door Or Window Alarm And A 120 dB Personal Alarm, Safety Essentials For College Students, Home Owners and Travelers For an apartment with only one door and one window that opens this set is great. But most places need a few more. For a dorm room this is fine. I've only seen dorm rooms that had one door and usually the dorm rooms windows are several stories up so it would probably be pretty hard for someone to enter that way. Unless it's on the ground floor.

The door stop alarm is extremely LOUD. And it will not stop SCREAMING until it is physically switched off. This is the first of this type I have ever tried out. A few years ago I bought about 10 door stop alarms of another brand and they were also very loud. However, once the pressure plate was released back up they would stop screaming. I guess it's good that it continues to scream until you stop it. Especially in a dorm type living situation. Someone would eventually come to see what was the matter. It takes one 9 volt battery.

The window alarm is extremely simple to install and the double sided sticky tape that comes with it is very strong. I have several of these window alarms attached to various windows at my home. They aren't the loudest but they should get the job done of scaring off an unwanted intruder. It takes 4 LR44 button batteries.

The personal key chain alarm is o.k. It's got a loud scream that makes my ears ring. It takes a good tug to pull out the pin to activate it. The small LED light is better than no light at all but don't expect a bright beam. It will help you find your keys if you dropped them in the dark. I think along with a sincere scream for help and the personal alarm screaming as well, I would think most aggressors would give up and try for an easier target.......at least I would hope so. It takes 3 LR44 button batteries.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Home Security Personal Safety Kit, Comes With A 120 dB Doorstop Alarm, 120 dB Door Or Window Alarm And A 120 dB Personal Alarm, Safety Essentials For College Students, Home Owners and Travelers

Alienware m15 R4 RTX 3070 Gaming Laptop Full HD (FHD), 15.6 inch - Intel Core i7-10870H, 16GB DDR4 RAM, 1TB SSD, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 8GB GDDR6, Windows 10 Home - Lunar Light First there is a cool factor of owning an Alienware product, the look and design of this laptop are several notches above what other laptops look like. I own MacBook 2020, and two other Dell laptops. This by far looks the coolest, but what we really care about is what's under the hood.

I was a bit concerned the display wasn't 4k but screen size is small enough to where it actually looks a bit sharper than my LG Ultrafine 4K displays. Color looks great.

I tried to run a user benchmark a few times with no luck for some reason. Wanted to see how it compared to my workstation. Tried updating drivers but still had issues with testing the GPU performance. So I decided to do an actual test with one of the tasks I do the most, video editing.

I recently bought a Dell workstation for editing a couple months ago and wanted to compare it with the m15 R4. My workstation specs i7-10700K, GeForce RTX 2060 Super, SSD, 32GB RAM. As a hobby I do a lot of video/photo editing. I have a couple decades of IT experience.

A little background. I switched to shooting in 4k 60 FPS with my DSLRs and drone footage. Even the most powerful consumer systems available 3-4 years ago have a hard time ripping these massive files and it's almost impossible to get any performance while editing. I use Adobe Premiere for all my video editing.

I took one of my more complicated Premiere projects and did a few tests. Both systems did a great job in edit, meaning little to no lag while scrolling through a massive timeline at 100% playback resolution. Once again this is 4K video all at 60FPS, need emphasize that.

Ripping/Rendering this 45 min project with GPU assistance took 37 mins on my workstation and 42 min on the M15. This same edit on my MacBook took just over 2 hours and was only half way at 4 hours with my older Dell laptops.

Overall very pleased with the video editing performance from the m15 As far as gaming goes my son plays fortnight and gets over 200 FPS with the M15.

Everything else works as expected. Multi color backlit keyboard looks great.
text_fidelity_b: Alienware m15 R4 RTX 3070 Gaming Laptop Full HD (FHD), 15.6 inch - Intel Core i7-10870H, 16GB DDR4 RAM, 1TB SSD, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 8GB GDDR6, Windows 10 Home - Lunar Light

I tried this camera as well as the Sony RX10 at my local camera store. The Panasonic has a noticeably longer zoom range, but the long end is much slower than the RX10, which makes your images noticeably worse in lower light conditions (like inside a camera store or any indoor conditions). The Panasonic is noticeably bulkier in your hand (about half an inch bigger in all dimensions). One comparison that the specs don't really tell you is that the build quality is significantly worse in the Panasonic compared to the Sony. The Sony RX10 has a metal frame and weather sealed shell and better overall fit-and-finish than the Panasonic. The poorer build quality of the Panasonic is reflected in the price, so you get what you pay for. Casual photographers may be happy with the Panasonic, but regular users will probably be happier with the Sony's more durable construction.

Jabra REVO Corded Stereo Headphones - Retail Packaging - Gray (Discontinued by Manufacturer) When I received the box I was extremely impressed with the sturdieness and attractiveness of the presentation. And although I know that many people don't care about such things, I happen to believe that if such concern is taken with the outside packaging - there is a very good chance the same attention to detail will pertain to the product itself. I was not wrong.

For someone who hasn't had a pair of "real" headphones since the early 80's, I was a little skeptical about the weight on my head, the quality of the sound, and the flexibility of something other than my earbuds. What a wonderful revelation. These headphones are extremely lightweight (in fact I wore them for about 2 hours straight and forgot I had them on when I was getting ready to leave the house), the cord that connects to your device is a very comfortable 48 inches long, they are flexible enough to conveniently fold down and place inside of a small pouch which is included, and as for the sound - it is simply incredible.

The ability to have the Jabra App convert most of my songs into an upgraded Dolby Digital Plus format at no additional cost is the real deal clincher. The music is breathtaking and made me wonder how I ever enjoyed the songs before these came along. Now I carry the little pouch in my purse and take them everywhere.

All I can say in conclusion is that if you really love your music and want to appreciate it at the highest level, for the price these are a wonderful investment. Save the earbuds for the gym, and use these headphones when you truly want to feel the music.

So beyond the lightning-fast bootup, it runs flawlessly! I hooked up a wireless mouse and keyboard set to it instead of the nice-looking wired set that comes with it. It handles the keyboard and mouse flawlessly. Honestly, I cannot think of a single bad thing to say about this pc! My last pc cost about $1,000 and had much crazier specs than this one but for the price point of this, I wish they would have had this Acer when I got my last desktop! Definitely get it, you will not regret it! I'm thinking of purchasing a 2nd one for my garage gym now so I can have access to all my music and everything easily. For the price point, why not?

text_fidelity_a:
Tripp Lite 550VA UPS Battery Backup, 300W Eco Green, USB, RJ11, 8 Outlets (ECO550UPS), Black The need for an uninterruptible power source is obvious to anyone with a computer or other expensive electronic equipment. The very day this product arrived, before I even opened the box, a severe thunderstorm knocked out power in my neighborhood. My two computers immediately went down and the screen on one kept flashing on and off even after all the power was dead. So yes, a UPS seems like an important piece of equipment these days. Sadly, this one is not for me. To be fair to the manufacturer though I need to give you a bit of context to help you evaluate if my reaction and this review would be applicable to you or not.

At age 70 I have a pretty low tolerance for muss and fuss. If it requires special handling, if it is a hassle to use, I don't want it. If it's not plug and play, I won't bother with it. For example, I do all my laundry in one load throwing everything in together without any sorting of any kind. It all gets washed and dried on the hot cycle. Anything that can't handle that gets tossed out. I treat everything like that. This UPS looks like an industrial strength product but acts like a delicate little snowflake. Coming out of the box it has 20 pages of instructions they want you to read before using. I didn't bother, just plugged it in, turned it on, and starting using the USB charger to juice up a battery run children's night light. A little while later I noticed a burnt plastic smell and saw the warping on the case that you can see in the attached photos. So this thing is not for me. More detail oriented and careful folks might have better luck with it. Thus I'm giving it a neutral 3 star rating and suggest you read through all the reviews here before deciding whether you want to try it yourself or not.
text_fidelity_b: Tripp Lite 550VA UPS Battery Backup, 300W Eco Green, USB, RJ11, 8 Outlets (ECO550UPS), Black

text_fidelity_a:
SIMOLIO 2.4G Analog Wireless TV Headsets with 100ft Transmit Range, No Pairing, No Delay, TV Voice Highlighting Headphones for Seniors, Wireless TV Headphones with Extra Soft Earbuds (SM-823 Pro) I began researching these based on reviewing another popular brand. I am a stickler for detail and after hours of research and asking questions I decided to give these a try because of the cost and positive reviews. I bought these for my elderly parent (90 years old) who has hearing loss but does not wear a hearing aid.
After a couple weeks of use I can honestly say these things are great! Very easy to install, easy to use for an elderly person not technically savvy, works from a long distance (we tried the next room), and the volume of these units can go very loud which is good for all types of hearing. There is also a balance control in case a person hears differently in both ears, and a switch to change from normal to higher or lower frequencies to help those with that type of hearing loss.
We can now watch TV when visiting my parent without the TV being so loud. But it is hard to verbally communicate with each other when they wear the headphones, but that’s not a big deal.
You can turn down the TV as low as needed, even muted, but the headphones can be as loud as needed. We used the RCA output from their TV (a 4 year old flat screen) and that works great. We tried it on a new flat screen and worked well also (digital output). All cables are provided along with extra ear inserts.
I like the fact this uses 2.4GHz instead of Bluetooth or infrared which often can lose connection with interference or movement away from the base station. I went out of the room into the next room and heard this one just fine.
The weight was a concern for me but my parent only watches TV for no more than 2 hours at the time and they said it was fine. There are ear loops provided to help with holding the unit if needed.
The only issue I found was that the input on the base station to charge the headphones was oriented backwards to how a person takes off the headset (have to turn the headset around to charge). And when putting on from the base station you have to turn the headphones around else you’ll put it on backwards which is not a big deal, but the volume button and balance will be reversed meaning my parent the first time turned the balance thinking it was volume and thought something was wrong. That’s one more thing for an elderly person to remember, plus you don’t need a lot of pressure to bend/break the charging prongs in the base unit if installed the wrong way.
We used the “speaker” option one time and it worked pretty well to allow a person to hear conversations in the room.

I’ll update this review should something change, but for now I highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: SIMOLIO 2.4G Analog Wireless TV Headsets with 100ft Transmit Range, No Pairing, No Delay, TV Voice Highlighting Headphones for Seniors, Wireless TV Headphones with Extra Soft Earbuds (SM-823 Pro)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony UBP-X800 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray Player Picture is nice,

The real reason I'm sending the units (I've had two) back, however, is that the player refuses to output the various high quality audio formats, including 7.1 DTS Master Audio. The digital coax cable barely works and the HDMI 2 audio output simply does not work, Admittedly I have an older receiver -- a Sony STR-DA5400ES, from 2009. But it has multiple HDMI inputs and the HDMI 2 audio output on the X800 is specifically designed to send audio to an older amp. Even Sony phone support says it should work. But it doesn't.. I spent 1 hour and 7 minutes with Sony ES support today going through every possible menu permutation on both the Amp and the UBP-X800 player. No luck The HDMI is dead. Zero output. The coax output can only send DTS EX 5.1, even though the player itself tells me it's playing DTS Master Audio 7.1.

This UBP-X800 has two HDMI outputs: one for video, one for audio. In case you don't have a 4K receiver with the ever-changing HDMI protocols, you're supposed to be able to feed HDMI audio to the amp. So I fed the video directly to the Samsung's video input (a direct cable connection) and another HDMI to my amp.

Zero audio from the player's HDMI audio feed. Not a peep of audio at all.

So I used the orange RCA digital audio coax connector to get surround sound audio.

But the coax digital audio cable only delivers DTS EX 5.1, not the 7.1 DTS Master Audio available on the Kingsman 4K disk. I updated the player's and the TV's firmware and read the manual. Nothing fixes the problem. Using all new, very short, high-speed HDMI 2.0 cables too.

My ancient Sony BDP-S560 Blu-ray player feeds all formats to the same 5400ES amp properly. I get great 7.1 DTS Master HD audio. Thus my old Blu-ray player sounds way better than my brand new advanced Sony UHD player.
Researching at the Sony forum under the UBP-X800 Audio Problems thread, answers were all over the place and none worked, I tried to register so I could post my problem and the website wouldn't allow me to. The comments there were complaining that they could not get the ATMOS tracks working.

I have no choice but to pack both X800s up and send them back.

Eventually I found that I needed to plug the 4K player into input 3 of the TV for the image to stabilize. Interesting that only some inputs on the TV can handle UHD source. But still, the player's audio doesn't work with my Sony Amp (Sony's fault).

HDMI was supposed to solve all these problems, but I suspect the HDCP copy protection schemes are really screwing things up or the firmware has bugs or companies just produce inferior products. Rather disappointing.
text_fidelity_b: Sony UBP-X800 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray Player

text_fidelity_a:
Zink Polaroid Snap Instant Digital Camera (Pink) with ZINK Zero Ink Printing Technology [[VIDEOID:fab011cbaf4d8ff273fb360a6d075448]] My granddaughter is too young to remember the big bulky Polaroid instant camera, so when I showed her this camera and told her it took instant pictures that she could use as stickers her comment was "AWESOME", and she's dying to get her hands on it. This compact sized 10 megapixel camera offers users the option of printing 2" x 3" photos instantly or adding up to a 32 GB micro SD card in order to store or share images.

The camera is straight forward and simple to use. If you want to take instant photos just load [[ASIN:B00ZSPI3A6 Polaroid 2x3 inch Premium ZINK Photo Paper TWIN PACK (20 Sheets) - Compatible With Polaroid Snap, Z2300, SocialMatic Instant Cameras & Zip Instant Printer]] into the chamber in the back of the camera, remove the magnetic lens cap, and gently press the viewfinder to turn the camera on.

Using the selector wheel at the top left, you can choose to take your photos in color, black & white, or sepia (which is like old time tin type for an antique look). Choose one, and then press the button next to that to select whether you want the photo to have a border or not. You can even press another button on the top to activate a 10 second delay to take selfies, and there's also a "photo booth mode" which takes a series of six quick pictures over the course of 10 seconds that you can set by depressing the shutter for three seconds.

Once you've chosen all of your desired options simply frame your shot in the viewfinder and press the shutter. There's no zoom or available adjustment, the camera automatically focuses and uses flash if needed, and the 2" x 3" print comes out of the side of the camera clear, sharp, and dry to the touch in under a minute. If you have film loaded the camera is going to print photos automatically when you press the shutter, so don't load paper if you prefer to use the micro SD card and not print. The camera has an auto sleep function that will shut it off to save battery power if sufficient times lapses between use, or you can just press the viewfinder back down to shut it off manually.

There are no instructions that comes with the camera, but you can read or print the manual yourself by going to polaroidsnapcamera dot come. You can also find the firmware update there. Be sure to charge the camera fully when you receive it, then insert a Micro SD card and update the firmware before using it. (Available here: http://polaroid.com/products/polaroid-snap-camera) Besides printing paper, you'll definitely want to have a MicroSD card for the camera and a case: [[ASIN:B017A1D6TI Polaroid Neoprene Pouch for The Polaroid Snap Instant Camera (Black)]].

There are several things about this product that could be improved on:
1. No sample printing paper included
2. No picture preview
3. No strap to attach the lens cover to which would help prevent losing it
4. Viewfinder pops open too easily
5. No instruction manual or link mention of the firmware update (or link to it) included with product

Otherwise, the camera is well made and fun to use. I can see where kids would have a lot of fun with this camera, but the photo paper isn't cheap so I may let my granddaughter use some and then just mostly use the Micro SD card. This could also be useful for producing instant photos at special events such as birthday parties, weddings, proms, and for other occasions, and the peel off backing on the photo paper makes it nice for scrap booking.

This instant camera was provided at no cost for my evaluation and review.
text_fidelity_b: Zink Polaroid Snap Instant Digital Camera (Pink) with ZINK Zero Ink Printing Technology

Samsung 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive Fit (MUF-128BB/AM) I bought 2 of these, they came today, and I and am returning them both tomorrow.

Chief reason: the drive is so small, that it is hard to plug into either USB port in the back of my new TV, a Sony XBR 850C. That TV has a somewhat constricted space where all of its ports are (USB, HDMI, etc). I just learned the hard way that I really need a longer drive to easily insert/remove it with this TV. Anyone else in a similar situation should likewise give this drive a serious rethink. I note that I had little problem with inserting/removing this drive from the front of my workstation, where I have unrestricted space.

Secondary reason: this drive has poor write speeds. My first transfer was of a single 2 GB movie file--a pure sequential write, which should be optimal--and yet I got an initial speed that started at ~50 MB/s and then it decay to maybe 40 MB/s. I should have paid more careful attention to the write benchmarks of this drive. I really want >= 100 MB/s write speeds.

It looks like my best bet is this drive's bigger brother, the Samsung 32GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive MUF-32BA/AM. Ordering 2 right now, stay tuned...
text_fidelity_b: Samsung 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive Fit (MUF-128BB/AM)

That said, I put my 400 songs on it and just let it play while I workout.

text_fidelity_a: SAMSUNG 34-Inch Odyssey G85SB Series QD-OLED Ultra WQHD Curved Gaming Monitor, 175Hz, 0.03ms, DisplayHDR True Black 400, AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, Advanced Game Streaming, LS34BG850SNXZA, 2023 Putting together this beast was not a very difficult task.  I am using the 'Ergotron – HX Single Ultrawide Monitor Arm' with this monitor.  There was a little bit of an odd feeling when it took me hooking both hdmi and display port up to figure out how to deal with the monitor source correctly.  This overall though is the most amazing monitor I've ever sat in front of.  I use this for engineering work as I'm not a gamer.  The screen real estate is much larger than typical 4k 1440p monitors.  The jump from a 34" to 49" was not as drastic of an impression as I would have expected.  The curve softens the hit to the senses as it seems a little shorter than it actually is.  The curve takes a little getting used to but it's not near as aggressive as people claim.  This is my first curved monitor because I didn't know if I could get used to it or not.  After a few hours of working on it, I barely notice anymore.  The picture is very clean and crisp.  I'm using it in conjunction with a sapphire card.  There are plenty of reviews about the exact specs of this monitor, but really I wanted to note that it shines when it comes to just immersing someone into the screen.  I only would suggest this to people that have a very deep measuring desk because this does take up quite a lot of room over the desk even with an arm holding it up.  Works well with Ubuntu 22.04 + Gnome + Wayland using a Sapphire Radeon Pulse RX 5600 XT which does PCIE 4.0 and has for a long time now.  The card actually handles it very easily at 120hz on gnome for daily grinds, fans are not even moving at the moment.  The booklet instructions are confusing, so while waiting for the monitor to ship I would suggest watching some unboxing.
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG 34-Inch Odyssey G85SB Series QD-OLED Ultra WQHD Curved Gaming Monitor, 175Hz, 0.03ms, DisplayHDR True Black 400, AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, Advanced Game Streaming, LS34BG850SNXZA, 2023

text_fidelity_a:
Linksys AC1900 Wi-Fi Wireless Dual-Band+ Router with Gigabit & USB 3.0 Ports, Smart Wi-Fi App Enabled to Control Your Network from Anywhere (EA6900) When I first set up a home network, I selected a Cisco "Linkys" G router (EA1300) because I recognized the brand name. Later I upgraded to a Cisco dual-band N router ([[ASIN:B007IL7AKM Linksys EA4500]]), which was--and still is--a superb router. My latest upgrade, to this LINKSYS AC1900 (EA6900) DUAL BAND SMART WI-FI ROUTER, represents another leap forward in the performance of my home network.

The wireless signal is stronger in every corner of my two-story condo. All of my devices (some 25 computers, tablets, music players, Kindles, cellphones, Roku, etc.) connect very quickly. Best of all, I'm getting Comcast's promised high-speed Internet speeds of more than 50 Mbps with the Comcast-supplied new telephony modem. (An online speed test site just now clocked the download speed at 57 Mbps). In fact, my present home network is capable of even faster speeds--the home network is limited by the speed of the slower external Comcast network.

This router is extremely easy to set up. You just connect it, and follow the prompts from the built-in software. Whenever you access the router to adjust the settings, and click on some part of the Menu, you find excellent "contextual" help screens that fully explain the meaning of each of the settings. The Menu is set up differently from the menus for the EA4500 and EA1300, but the basic methodology for the settings is the same--the settings are just presented in a way that's easier for a non-techie user to understand.

I read a newspaper review that recommended NOT buying this excellent EA6900 router, because of testers' problems with the second band and with nonfunctioning USB ports. I think that the testers probably received a defective router--and should have requested a replacement. Even a reliable brand like Cisco may sometimes ship an occasional bad electronics device.

Because I only need a single-band router, I haven't tested the second band on my EA6900 router. (The second band did work fine on my EA4500 router, but using the second band didn't improve the signal strength, so I didn't continue using it.) However, I did test the USB ports on the EA6900, and both work really well. In fact, the router recognized and easily accessed a couple of external wireless storage drives--connected with a 100-foot (!) USB cable--when my PC was flakey about recognizing those same drives when they were connected directly to the PC with the long cable.

I absolutely love this EA6900 router, which I've been using for more than a month now. Because of my home wiring, the router is located a long way from any of my wireless devices, and I have a lot of nearby neighbors with competing wireless Internet connections. But with the EA6900, there have been virtually no dropped connections, and the strong signal is something that I've long been wishing for!
text_fidelity_b: Linksys AC1900 Wi-Fi Wireless Dual-Band+ Router with Gigabit & USB 3.0 Ports, Smart Wi-Fi App Enabled to Control Your Network from Anywhere (EA6900)

Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Black Colorful Retro 2.4GHz Typewriter with Cute Round Keycaps, DPI Adjustable Optical Compatible PC Laptop Heat is the main killer of computers and computer equipment so keeping a system cool and ventilated is a big deal, especially when involving systems that see heavy use. Laptops are just as vulnerable as larger servers and require the same precautions. One of the main solutions for heat dissipation and ventilation for laptops is a chill pad (a fan-based platform that moves air under the system) and this one by AMNIE has been outstanding. I have been using it for about two weeks on my personal system and likely will swap it over to the system in the house that sees the heaviest use.

This is a good-sized pad, able to comfortably handle laptops up to 17”. It has a total of 4 larger fans that move some serious amounts of air, and fans are paired two and two between a pair of switches. The frame is painted metal mesh and offers good support to the laptop it holds.

The switches that control the fans are dial controls and they provide variable fan speeds for each pair of fans they control. There are no graduations so you can set the speed anywhere within the range to suit you, though having that much control is probably not all that necessary. The fans run very quiet but on the highest speed setting really move the air. When maxed out and all four fans running at top speed the fans blew cooler air from between the frame and the laptop, telling me I had the speed up much higher than needed. For my particular system under my typical use load, it seems I only need to turn them on about half way.

I have worked with some chill pads that have flaws in either the fans or the bearings and they make awful amounts of noise. So far, the only noise this pad makes is a low-frequency hum. It is quiet enough that even with lower-end noise canceling headphones I can cancel out the noise completely. This pad is not silent even on the low end of fan speed but it is very quiet all the way through the range of speeds. I have been able to leave the fans on full speed all night and sleep through the sound.

I have not measured the temperature difference between when the fans are on vs. when they are not, but I have noticed that the internal fan does not kick in as frequently when doing video rendering as when the fans are off. It does turn on and it still hits high speed on occasion but it is noticeably less frequently.

This is an excellent chill pad for laptops and so far it has worked out exceptionally well for me. It is quiet, it moves a lot of air and my laptop’s internal fan does not kick in as high as often. text_fidelity_a:
iHome 2-In-1 Pen Stylus for iPad/iPad 2 and all Touch Screen Devices (IH-IP2202) I expect that no one is going to use a stylus 100% of the time with their touch screen. There are, however, some times when a stylus is more convenient than using your finger. Drawing objects freehand is a common example. Another example is when you need to precisely move objects around the screen (eg in a CAD program) and this is difficult with your finger because your finger blocks your view of the target area.

There are many many touch screen stylus for sale on Amazon. Some cost less than 50 cents each. All the latest stylus have similar round soft touch rubber tips. All seem to work about the same. This iHome stylus doesn't seem to work any better than the others that I have tried.

The iHome stylus is better looking than most of the competition because of the long slim shape with silver-tone accents. Some of the cheap ones look very plasticy (though they do work just as well). Some other stylus are fatter, which makes them easier to grip if you have large hands.

The built-in ball-point pen is a feature that most other stylus do not have. The pen works well, though I do not know how easy ink refills will be to find. There is no literature in the package about what refills it can use.

Is this product worth $15? I have to say no, but I'm a cheapskate. You can decide on value for yourself, but look at the competition first.
text_fidelity_b: iHome 2-In-1 Pen Stylus for iPad/iPad 2 and all Touch Screen Devices (IH-IP2202)

text_fidelity_a:
Zell Technologies USB-C 12 Port Docking Station, 100W Power Delivery Dock, 12-in-1 Double Display 4k USB C Docking Station Dual Monitor USB C Hub Dual Displayport and HDMI I am using the Zell Technologies USB-C 12 Port Docking Station right now as I write this review. I’ve had the dock on my desk for about three weeks now and like it a lot. My desk looks neater, the dock gives me all the ports I need on a daily basis without having to use multiple adapters, and it charges my laptop.

I didn’t need to download any extra drivers or software, the dock was plug and play for me. I’m using it with my Intel MacBook Pro (13-inch, 2017, Thunderbolt 3 ports). I had the ports replaced once but they are loose again, so a dock is extra useful for me -- I’m only plugging in one device instead of 3 or 4. And I don’t have to look for adapters for everything I want to plug in.

I have one external monitor plugged into the dock, using the HDMI port. I also tried connecting via DisplayPort and that worked just fine. I also have various USB peripherals plugged in. I like the arrangement of ports, most are in the back, but the dock has a USB 3.0 port as well as Micro SD and SD ports on the front, where you can easily swap flash drives and cards.

The only USB-C port is for connecting the dock to your computer. I would’ve liked a USB-C port to accommodate newer flash drives and phones, but that’s just because of my port problem on my laptop.

For my usage, mostly writing and streaming shows, the dock does not run hot.
text_fidelity_b: Zell Technologies USB-C 12 Port Docking Station, 100W Power Delivery Dock, 12-in-1 Double Display 4k USB C Docking Station Dual Monitor USB C Hub Dual Displayport and HDMI

All have performed just fine, but this new stick has some major improvements that I really like.

Setup was as easy as with other Fire devices -- it walks you through the steps on screen. It also does a setup for having the remote control the TV and the receiver (my Fire Stick is plugged into my AV receiver). It works great -- I can power on/off both the TV (Samsung) and receiver (Onkyo) by just pressing the power button on the Fire remote. During power-up it also sets the receiver to the correct port for using the Fire stick. The volume on the remote controls the volume on the receiver. Very handy feature that works every time.

The overall speed and responsiveness is improved over earlier Fire sticks. Menus are more snappy and apps load faster. There are also a number of new settings to control audio and video aspects. I left most on their default, but it's nice to be able to get into the settings and tweak them.

A very nice upgrade to the Fire line. 100% satisfied with the purchase!

CyberPower CP685AVRLCD Intelligent LCD UPS System, 685VA/390W, 8 Outlets, AVR, Compact When I had a power outage right in the middle of a Windows Update I deceided I had to get a UPS. I spend a lot of time researching my options. This unit seemed like the best deal providing an LCD readout and the ability to easily turn of all alarms.

Unit is well built. Documentation is adequate. Easy to set up. I did not install the provided computer software, as the LCD screen on the unit gives me plenty of information.

When connections were complete and everything powered on (HP slimline desktop Computer, Modem, Router and 23" LED Monitor to the batttery outlets) the readout indicated I was only using 40% of the UPS output and that I could expect a battery back-up of 22 minutes. I highly recommend this unit. For the price, it cannot be beat!

Typically any device requiring an Ethernet cable will come with one in the packaging - it will work (usually). A good comparison is those cables are much like an old car - it should get you there, whereas these cables are like a high end sports car - they will get you there lightning fast, without failure.

The Cat8 cables in this set are much thinner than many others but don’t let that dissuade you as in all of my testing over the last 5 months has shown this cable set performs flawlessly. These cables are designed to really hold up.

The connector bases are reinforced at each end of the wire which really help hold all of the wires in place even if you have to bend and twist it to fit it within the plug. The connector plug itself is gold plated which is the ultimate standard in connectivity.

This Cat8 Ethernet Cable is 10’ long which makes it absolutely ideal for using it to directly plug your computer or gaming system into your router. So many of us stream programs and movies via our TV or computer and there is no comparison in speed between a WiFi connection and a wired connection. For gamers, it is absolutely the way to go - do away with all lag caused by your WiFi by connecting directly to your router.

You will not find a better set of 10’ Ethernet Cables - this is really a top of the line Ethernet cable set that you’ll love.

This is a purchase that you’ll never regret.

They take up less floor space, are easier to tuck away, and can also go on a table or desk.  This is a good one of that sort of product. The outlets are spaced far apart and obviously on different faces, so you don't have any issues with plugging in those overside adaptors that some any items come with nowadays. That's a big plus all by itself.  This also has two USB ports which means you don't have to take up an outlet with a charger. It's modular, so you can separate it into two pieces if you want. And you can also turn off half the items you have plugged in and leave the other half on if you want--that flexibility is nice.  And it looks good as well.  It's light, which is both good and bad--if you put it on a desk and have heavy cords hanging off it may slide or need to be weighted down/blocked. But that's a minor issue and one that's not going to happen in most cases.  Very pleased with this.

Echo Show 15 | Full HD 15.6" smart display with Alexa and Fire TV built in | Remote included So honestly I wish these kind of screen models is what amazon did the entire time. It arrived the same day i ordered it. And hanging it up was very simple and quick.

Good:
1. Decent sound actually enjoy the speakers while playing music.
2. Touch screen pretty responsive
3. Many video app choices
4. Nice security features by setting up doorbell or camera settings in alexa app...depends on your devices but we have wyze cameras and a ring door bell and its given me what i wanted it for in terms of seeing whos at the door on the screen quickly vs my actual security system panel which is very slow.

Bad
1. limited widgets so far
2. cant install any kind of app
3. The dance between what is setup though the machine and what is setup on your app is annoyingly confusing with no really any direction for the user.
4. Profiles...in general a good thing but no matter what i did things were never as "personalized" as promised so we just ignored the feature. Especially the calendar which I eventually got working but in the end just decided to delete my wifes profile and combine a calendar...things like sticky notes and shopping lists arent unique or we couldnt figure out how...yet i could tell alexa to sent my wife a note...
5. Camera needs work in general...someones visual id was great but it seems mostly hit or miss as you walk toward the machine.

Future
1. I wish all profiles were directly linked to actual accounts...regardless of house hold...make it truly personalized. Signing into an account should be step one of adding a new profile.
2. I hope they go a tad bigger 15" is nice but maybe something in the 20's
3. App installs even if only from amazon app store.
4. widget pages aka just more room...i know some will be hidden but just let us swipe like a smart phone
